Conduct the cross superlet transform on a time series or signal

Source: R/analyse_Xsuperlet.R, R/zzz_aliases_american.R
analyse_Xsuperlet.Rd

Compute the cross superlet transform using a complex Morlet wavelet based on the approach of Moca et al. (2021) and the "analyze.coherency" function of the WaveletComp package. The superlet transform increases time frequency resolution by combining multiple wavelet orders at each frequency.

Usage

analyse_Xsuperlet(
  data_1 = NULL,
  data_2 = NULL,
  upperPeriod = 1024,
  lowerPeriod = 2,
  Nf = 128,
  c1 = 3,
  o = c(1, 10),
  mult = TRUE,
  order_scaling = "log2",
  order_alpha = 1,
  verbose = FALSE,
  detrend = "linear",
  standardize = TRUE,
  standardise = NULL,
  wavelet = "morlet",
  wavelet_order = NULL
)

analyze_Xsuperlet(
  data_1 = NULL,
  data_2 = NULL,
  upperPeriod = 1024,
  lowerPeriod = 2,
  Nf = 128,
  c1 = 3,
  o = c(1, 10),
  mult = TRUE,
  order_scaling = "log2",
  order_alpha = 1,
  verbose = FALSE,
  detrend = "linear",
  standardize = TRUE,
  standardise = NULL,
  wavelet = "morlet",
  wavelet_order = NULL
)

Arguments

data_1

First record: a matrix or data frame with depth/time in column 1 and the proxy value in column 2. Both records are sorted, rows with NA are removed and they are interpolated to a common, regular grid over their overlapping interval (spacing: the coarser of the two median sampling intervals); at least 10 common points are needed. Required (Default=NULL gives an error).

data_2

Second record, in the same format and depth/time unit as data_1 (matrix or data frame: depth/time in column 1, proxy value in column 2). The cross phase is the phase of data_1 minus that of data_2. Required (Default=NULL gives an error).

upperPeriod

Longest period to analyse, in the same unit as the depth/time column of the records (numeric, > lowerPeriod); sets the lowest analysed frequency. Default=1024.

lowerPeriod

Shortest period to analyse, in the same unit as the depth/time column of the records (numeric, > 0; at least twice the common sampling interval); sets the highest analysed frequency. Default=2.

Nf

Number of frequencies of the superlet spectrum (integer, >= 1). Frequencies are logarithmically spaced between 1/upperPeriod and 1/lowerPeriod. Default=128.

c1

Base number of cycles of the Morlet wavelet of order 1 (numeric, > 0, typically 2 to 5): the fundamental wavelet width. Default=3.

o

Minimum and maximum superlet order (numeric vector of length 2, values >= 1), from the lowest to the highest frequency; a single number gives a fixed order and NULL uses order 1 everywhere (see analyse_superlet). Default=c(1, 10).

mult

How the number of cycles grows with the order i within a superlet (logical, TRUE or FALSE): TRUE multiplicative (\(c_i = i c_1\)); FALSE additive (\(c_i = c_1 + i - 1\), Moca et al., 2021). Default=TRUE.

order_scaling

How the superlet order increases from o[1] (lowest frequency) to o[2] (highest frequency) (character): "none" or "log2" (linear in log2(frequency)), "linear" (linear in frequency), "sqrt", "quadratic" or "power" (see analyse_superlet). Default="log2".

order_alpha

Exponent of the "power" order scaling (numeric, > 0); only used when order_scaling="power". Values greater than 1 raise the order mainly at the highest frequencies (sharpening short periods), values smaller than 1 already at low frequencies. Default=1.

verbose

Print the sampling interval to which each record was interpolated and show progress bars (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

detrend

Removal of a trend from both records before the transform, passed to analyse_superlet (character): "linear", "mean" or "none". Default="linear".

standardize

Divide both (detrended) records by their standard deviation before the transform, passed to analyse_superlet (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=TRUE.

standardise

British spelling of standardize (logical); if given (not NULL) it overrides standardize. Default=NULL.

wavelet

Mother wavelet (character string or function), given as a name (PyWavelets style names with the order appended, such as "db4", "sym8", "cgau3", "gaus2" or "cmor1.5-1", also work) or as a function psi_hat(omega) that returns the Fourier transform of a user defined mother wavelet. Analytic (complex) wavelets, which give phase and amplitude and can be synchrosqueezed: "morlet" (default; aliases "gabor", "amor"), "morlet0" (exactly zero mean Morlet, admissible for a small omega_nr; alias "morlex"), "paul" (alias "cauchy"), "morse" (generalised Morse wavelet of Olhede and Walden, 2002; aliases "gmw", "airy"), "bump", "cmor" (complex Morlet with bandwidth and centre frequency as in Matlab/PyWavelets), "cgau" (analytic Gaussian derivative; "cmhat" is the complex Mexican hat), "shannon" (complex Shannon, box spectrum), "fbsp" (frequency B-spline), "meyer", "loggabor" (alias "lognormal"), "gammatone" (asymmetric in time: sharp onset, slow decay) and "hann" (raised cosine band). Real wavelets, which give a real transform (no phase or envelope): "dog" (derivative of Gaussian; "mexh", "ricker", "marr" and "sombrero" are the Mexican hat, order 2), "morl" (real Morlet), "hhat" (Hermitian hat), "poisson", and the orthogonal wavelets "haar", "db" (Daubechies), "sym" (Symlets) and "battle" (Battle-Lemarie spline wavelets), which are computed in the frequency domain from their filters. The period axis of the orthogonal wavelets is approximate because their spectra are broad and not symmetric. A narrow wavelet (Paul, low-order DOG, Shannon, Haar) resolves position well, a wide one (Morse with a large beta, Morlet with a high omega_nr, bump) resolves period well. Default="morlet".

wavelet_order

Parameter(s) of the wavelet (see analyse_superlet): paul: order m (default 4); dog: derivative m (default 2); morse: c(gamma, beta) or beta alone with gamma = 3 (default c(3, 20)); bump: c(mu, sigma) (default c(5, 0.6)); cmor: c(bandwidth, centre frequency) (default c(1.5, 1)); cgau: derivative m (default 4); shannon: c(bandwidth, centre frequency) (default c(2, 1.5)); fbsp: c(m, bandwidth, centre frequency) (default c(2, 2, 1.5)); loggabor: c(centre angular frequency, log-width) (default c(6, 0.25)); meyer and hhat have no parameter; morlet0: omega_0 (default omega_nr); morl: omega_0 (default 5); poisson: order n (default 2); gammatone: c(n, centre angular frequency, bandwidth) (default c(4, 6, 1.5)); hann: c(centre angular frequency, half width) (default c(6, 3)); db: number of vanishing moments 1 to 20 (default 4, "haar" = "db1"); sym: 2 to 20 (default 8); battle: spline order 1, 3, 5 or 7 (default 3). Passed to analyse_superlet; for the Morlet wavelet the number of cycles is set by c1, o and mult. Default=NULL.

Value

A list with class "analyze.Xsuperlet" containing Wave: complex wavelet coefficients Power: time frequency power spectrum dt: sampling interval after interpolation Phase: instantaneous phase of the signal dj: number of frequencies Power.avg: average spectral power Period: physical periods corresponding to frequencies nc: number of columns in the input data nr: number of frequency levels axis.1: x axis values (time or depth) axis.2: y axis values (log2 scaled periods) c1: base number of wavelet cycles o: numeric vector of length two defining the minimum and maximum superlet order. If NULL, all frequencies are analysed using order one. x1: interpolated x values first data set y1: interpolated signal values first data set x2: interpolated x values second data set y2: interpolated signal values second data set

References

Moca, V. V., Bârzan, H., Nagy-Dăbâcan, A., & Mureșan, R. C. (2021). Time-frequency super-resolution with superlets. Nature Communications, 12(1), 337. doi:10.1038/s41467-020-20539-9

Author

The "analyse_Xsuperlet" that generates the input for the plotting function is based on the matlab code in Moca et al. (2021) and the the "analyze.coherency" function of the 'WaveletComp' R package

Examples

# \donttest{
#Example 1. A cross superlet of two etp solutions with noise overprint
etp_1 <- astrochron::etp(
 tmin = 0,
 tmax = 300,
 dt = 1,
 eWt = 1.5,
 oWt = 0.75,
 pWt = 1,
 esinw = TRUE,
 standardize = TRUE,
 genplot = FALSE,
 verbose = FALSE
)

etp_2 <- astrochron::etp(
 tmin = 0,
 tmax = 300,
 dt = 1,
 eWt = 1,
 oWt = 0.5,
 pWt = 1.5,
 esinw = TRUE,
 standardize = TRUE,
 genplot = FALSE,
 verbose = FALSE
)

etp_1[, 2] <- etp_1[, 2] + wr_coloured_noise(
 nrow(etp_1),
 sd = sd(etp_1[, 2]) / 1.5,
 mean = mean(etp_1[, 2]),
 phi = 0.9
)
etp_2[, 2] <- etp_2[, 2] + wr_coloured_noise(
 nrow(etp_2),
 sd = sd(etp_2[, 2]) / 1.5,
 mean = mean(etp_2[, 2]),
 phi = 0.9
)

Xetp <- analyse_Xsuperlet(
 data_1 = etp_1,
 data_2  = etp_2,
 upperPeriod = 256,
 lowerPeriod = 2,
 Nf = 32,
 c1 = 3,
 o = c(1, 10),
 mult = TRUE,
 order_scaling = "log2",
 order_alpha = 1,
 verbose = FALSE
)
# }
